task: This is a synthetic newspaper-writing exercise using fictional reporting notes. Use only the supplied reporting notes. Write from the reporting snapshot as of August 31, 2026. Write a headline and a 450–650-word AP-style newspaper explainer about Moorfin Bank's tiered savings offer, answering how the advertised top rate applies to a customer with a larger balance.

facts.text: Moorfin Bank introduced its Step Saver account in August 2026 with a headline annual rate of 4% on the first $2,000.
Balances above $2,000 earn 0.2% annually under the supplied rate schedule.
The account credits interest once a year and calculates it from daily principal balances under each tier.

The bank's illustration assumes a constant $10,000 daily principal balance, qualifying payroll deposits in every month and unchanged rates for a year; it produces $80 on the first $2,000 and $16 on the remaining $8,000.
The illustration totals $96 in annual interest, equal to 0.96% of the starting $10,000 rather than 4% of the whole balance.
The example excludes changes in principal and does not promise the variable rates will remain unchanged for a year.
The top tier requires at least one qualifying payroll deposit each month; without it, that month's calculation uses the account's 0.1% fallback rate on all principal.
Transfers from another savings account do not count as payroll deposits under the bank's stated definition.
The account has no monthly maintenance fee in the supplied schedule.
Its stated variable-rate notice process is separate from its annual interest-crediting date.
Branch manager Tera Quill says the product is intended to attract regular payroll relationships rather than large passive balances alone.
Quill said, "The four percent has a boundary around it: the first two thousand dollars and the qualifying deposits."
Customer Oren Selt keeps a reserve for irregular household repairs and initially multiplied his whole balance by the advertised rate.
Selt said, "I was comparing the big number on the poster before I understood which part of my money it described."
The bank's account illustration is not a comparison against every competing account or investment.
A customer with exactly $2,000 and all qualifying deposits would have a different blended result from the $10,000 illustration.
The reporting record does not supply tax treatment for an individual customer's interest.
Customers can obtain a printed tier schedule at the branch rather than relying only on the promotional sign.
Moorfin has nine branches and introduced its first payroll-linked current account in 2015.
No source in the packet recommends a particular account for every reader's circumstances.

forbidden_additions: 4% on the entire $10,000 or a guaranteed $96 regardless of rate and balance changes
Every incoming transfer qualifies as payroll or the account is best for every reader

The $96 illustration combines $80 and $16 from different balance tiers.
